title: What CPD do real estate agents need in NSW for 2026-27?
description: NSW property agent CPD for 2026-27: compulsory topics and minimum hours by area of practice, the Class 1 forum and AUSTRAC course, records and exemptions.
shortAnswer: Real estate agents in New South Wales must complete continuing professional development (CPD) every year from 1 July to 30 June. For 2026-27, Class 1 and Class 2 licensees complete compulsory topics set for each area of practice they work in, usually 7 hours with an approved provider, and Class 1 licensees add a 5 hour NSW Fair Trading accredited forum and AUSTRAC's real estate AML/CTF course. Assistant agents complete three Certificate IV units.
keyTakeaways: The NSW CPD year runs from 1 July to 30 June. Requirements are set by license category and by the areas of practice a person actually works in, not by the full scope the license permits.

Residential salespeople need at least 7 hours covering four compulsory topics: auction laws and practice, contracts, Rules of Conduct refresher, and Supervision Guidelines and AML CTF in agency practice.
Residential property managers need at least 7 hours on three topics, including Domestic and Family Violence delivered for a minimum of 4 hours by a provider approved for that course.

Compulsory topics must be interactive (face to face with up to 40 attendees, or webinar with up to 25), delivered by a provider approved by the Strata and Property Services Commissioner, and include an assessment activity.
Licensees keep CPD records for 3 years and certificate holders for 4 years. Non-compliance can lead to suspension or cancellation and a court penalty of up to $11,000.
jurisdiction: Australia (New South Wales): Property and Stock Agents Act 2002
regulator: NSW Fair Trading and the Strata and Property Services Commissioner
appliesTo: Class 1 and Class 2 real estate licensees (residential sales, property management, buyers agents, commercial agents, business brokers, onsite residential property managers)
Strata managing agents and stock and station agents
Assistant agents holding a certificate of registration
Licensees-in-charge, who must hold an agency training plan
Training providers approved to deliver compulsory CPD topics

sections.heading: How does the NSW property CPD scheme work?

blocks.text: Every Class 1 licensee, Class 2 licensee and certificate of registration holder must complete the CPD set for their category each year. NSW Fair Trading's [CPD requirements page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/property-professionals/working-as-an-agent/continuing-professional-development) (last updated 9 July 2026) defines two dimensions: the license category held (real estate, stock and station, or strata managing agent) and the area of practice in which the person operates.

Within the real estate category there are six areas of practice: residential sales, residential property management, buyers agents, commercial real estate, business brokers and onsite (short-term) residential property managers. A licensee who works in only one area completes only that area's compulsory topics. Someone working across several completes the topics for each, without repeating a topic that is shared, as long as every area's learning outcomes are met.
There is no carry-over between years for licensees. The only exception is for assistant agents, who can carry forward extra Certificate IV units completed in a CPD year.

blocks.text: The Domestic and Family Violence course for property managers carries an extra condition: it may only be delivered where NSW Fair Trading has reviewed the course content and assessment material, so agencies should check that their provider is approved for that specific course before enrolling staff.

blocks.title: Primary text: NSW Fair Trading
blocks.text: "You may need to complete more than the minimum CPD hours for one area of practice to meet all required learning outcomes."

sections.heading: What extra CPD do Class 1 licensees need?

blocks.text: Class 1 licensees have two additional obligations on top of their core hours. First, they must spend at least 5 hours at a NSW Fair Trading accredited forum relevant to their license category; dual license holders attend only one forum in the year. NSW Fair Trading runs several forums in 2026-27, and some approved providers also offer accredited sessions, which may carry a fee.

Second, Class 1 licensees in residential sales, buyers agency, commercial real estate, business broking and stock and station agency must complete AUSTRAC's "Smart real estate agent's guide to AML/CTF" course, either online (all three modules) or through AUSTRAC's train-the-trainer model, and keep evidence of completion. NSW Fair Trading is explicit that this does not replace the compulsory Supervision Guidelines and AML/CTF topic delivered by approved providers. For the federal AML/CTF obligations behind this, see [AML/CTF training for real estate agents](/regulations/aml-ctf-tranche-2-real-estate-training).

sections.heading: Who can deliver NSW compulsory CPD, and in what format?

blocks.text: Only a training provider approved by the Strata and Property Services Commissioner can deliver compulsory topics. The approved list for 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 is published on the Fair Trading page under the Property and Stock Agents Act 2002.

items: Delivery must be interactive: face to face with no more than 40 attendees, or an interactive webinar with no more than 25.
Every compulsory topic must include an assessment activity.
Licensees-in-charge must have all CPD training set out in the agency's training plan.

Assistant agents instead complete at least 3 units each year from the Certificate IV required for a Class 2 license in real estate, strata management or stock and station, and keep the RTO statement of attainment for each unit.

sections.heading: What records, exemptions and penalties apply?

blocks.text: Licensees keep their own records of compulsory topics completed and produce them if NSW Fair Trading asks. Class 1 and Class 2 licensees keep records for 3 years; certificate of registration holders keep them for 4 years.

A person whose license or certificate commenced less than 90 days before the end of the CPD year is exempt for that year; for 2026-27 that means a commencement on or after 1 April 2027. The exemption does not apply where CPD is a condition imposed after suspension or cancellation. NSW Fair Trading warns that failing to meet CPD requirements can lead to suspension or cancellation and a court penalty of up to $11,000.

sections.heading: How should an NSW agency evidence CPD compliance?

blocks.text: An agency's CPD record should be organized by person and area of practice, because that is how the requirement is set. sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each area of practice as a set of learning outcomes, so an agent working across sales and property management sees one plan with shared topics counted once, matching how NSW Fair Trading credits overlap. The licensee-in-charge's training plan is generated from the same map. See [professional services](/industries/professional-services).

faqs.q: Does a residential salesperson in NSW need to complete property management CPD?
faqs.a: Not if they do not work in property management. NSW Fair Trading says a real estate licensee who operates in one area of practice completes only that area's mandatory modules, even though the license may authorize other areas. If they also manage properties, they must complete the property management topics as well.

faqs.q: Can unused NSW CPD hours be carried into next year?
faqs.a: No, for licensees. The NSW arrangements do not allow carry-over from one CPD year to the next, except for assistant agents, who may carry forward additional Certificate IV units completed during the year.

faqs.q: Does an online self-paced course count as NSW compulsory CPD?
faqs.a: Compulsory topics must be delivered interactively by an approved provider, either face to face with up to 40 attendees or by interactive webinar with up to 25, and must include an assessment activity. The AUSTRAC course for Class 1 licensees is a separate requirement and can be completed through AUSTRAC's self-paced eLearning.

faqs.q: What if a NSW agent gets their license late in the CPD year?
faqs.a: If the license or certificate commenced less than 90 days before the CPD year ends, the holder is exempt for that year. For 2026-27, a license commencing on or after 1 April 2027 is automatically exempt, although the holder remains responsible for keeping their knowledge current.

factCheck.claim: CPD year runs 1 July to 30 June; requirements depend on licence category and area of practice; six real estate areas of practice; shared topics not repeated; no carry-over except assistant agents; page last updated 9 July 2026.

2026-27 compulsory topics and minimum hours: residential sales 7 hours, 4 topics; property managers 7 hours incl. DFV minimum 4 hours; buyers agents 7; commercial 7; business brokers 7; onsite 4; strata 6; stock and station 7.

Compulsory topics delivered by providers approved by the Strata and Property Services Commissioner, interactive face to face (max 40) or webinar (max 25), with an assessment activity; DFV courses only where content reviewed by NSW Fair Trading.

Class 1 licensees must attend a minimum 5 hour accredited forum (one for dual licensees) and Class 1 licensees in relevant areas must complete AUSTRAC's Smart real estate agent's guide to AML/CTF; this does not replace the compulsory AML/CTF topic.

Records kept 3 years for licensees and 4 years for certificate holders; 90 day exemption (licence commencing on or after 1 April 2027 exempt for 2026/27); assistant agents complete 3 Certificate IV units; penalty up to $11,000 plus suspension or cancellation.
